objective: Learners compute invented net cash flow across two simulated months, including a deficit, and evaluate the combined position.
scenario: Lars is a made-up seventh grader building a pretend cash-flow statement. In invented month one, inflows are $1,850.00 and outflows are $1,920.00. In month two, inflows rise to $2,050.00 with the same outflows. All figures are invented.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Compute the net cash flow for Lars's invented month one.

prompts.text: What is the net cash flow in month one?

tasks.directions: Compute month two's net cash flow with the higher inflows, then combine the two months into a single position.

prompts.text: What is the net cash flow in month two?
What is the combined net cash flow across both months?

tasks.directions: A third invented month brings inflows of $1,700.00 with outflows unchanged.

prompts.text: What is the net cash flow in month three?
What is the combined position across all three months?

tasks.directions: A positive month sat between two negative ones.

prompts.text: Explain why looking at a single month of cash flow can mislead, and what the three-month position tells Lars that month two alone did not.

remediation: If a learner drops the negative sign, write Lars's inflows and outflows in two columns and mark the direction of the difference before recording it.
extension: Ask the learner what outflow level would make all three of Lars's invented months at least break even, and to show the reasoning.
